notes: Track 1 Tier 1 — deterministic tool-calling battery. Single source of truth for case
definitions, shared by sweep_toolcall.py (execution) and grade_sweep.py (grading).
The driver copies this file into the run dir so a harvested run grades self-contained.
SAMPLING: temperature 0 (greedy), NOT the battery's thinking profile (temp 1.0). Tool
calling is a pass/fail binary, so at temp 1.0 with n=1 you cannot separate 'model can't'
from 'unlucky sample'. Greedy is also what BFCL and friends use, which is what makes a
low score here comparable to a vendor's published claim instead of noise.
enable_tools:false is sent on every request. That suppresses SERVER-SIDE built-ins (web
search, code exec) — a different mechanism from the client-tool passthrough under test.
Belt-and-braces with --disable-tools at launch; contamination is caught by the per-case
PROMPT-TOKEN CEILINGS are per-case (expect.max_prompt_tokens), not global. Prompt size
scales with how many tool schemas a case offers -- tc_distractor legitimately costs ~775
tokens for its 5 schemas, where tc_single costs ~340. A single global threshold flags the
distractor case as contaminated on every run. Real server-side injection ran 2000-16000,
so a ~2x-baseline ceiling separates the two without false positives.

tc_single.intent: Correct function selection + valid JSON args when exactly one tool fits.
tc_single.prompt: What is the current temperature in Denver? Use the available tool; do not guess.

function.name: get_weather
function.description: Get the current weather for a city.

tc_distractor.intent: Five tools offered, exactly one correct. Catches models that pattern-match the first tool or the most recently described one.
tc_distractor.prompt: How much is 250 US dollars in euros right now? Use the available tools.

tc_refusal.intent: No offered tool fits. The model must answer directly rather than hallucinate a call. A get_weather('Paris') here is the classic failure.
tc_refusal.prompt: What is the capital city of France?

tc_chain.intent: Multi-turn: the tool result must actually be consumed. The count 4731 is unguessable, so a correct 9462 cannot be produced without reading the tool response.
tc_chain.prompt: Look up how many units of SKU AX-19 are in stock, then tell me what that count would be if it were doubled. State the doubled number on its own line as 'RESULT: <n>'.

function.name: get_inventory_count
function.description: Get the current in-stock unit count for a SKU.

tc_longchain.intent: Regression for ggml-org/llama.cpp#19513 — premature EOS after roughly 10-20 sequential tool calls. Reported against Qwen3-Coder-Next, MiniMax-M2 and GLM-4.5-Air. Pass = survives 15 chained calls.
tc_longchain.prompt: Call step with n=0. It returns the next value of n. Keep calling step with the value it returns, one call at a time, until it returns done=true. Then report the token it gives you on its own line as 'TOKEN: <token>'. Do not skip ahead and do not guess the token.

function.name: step
function.description: Advance the counter by one and return the next value of n.
